rows.name: RUNNER_NAME

problems.statement: `prime_hf_models.py`, the CI script that downloads the pinned Hugging Face model snapshots (`bin/ci/prime_hf_models.py`)
problems.code_says: The read is in the function cache_context. The download script calls it, and bin/ci/ingest/snapshots.py calls it too (require_model_snapshots). bin/ci/ingest/prepare_tests.py and bin/ci/model-traces/prepare_inputs.py run that path in gcp-nix.yml jobs, so the cache_context log line with the runner name also appears in those job logs.

cells.Where: `prime_hf_models.py`, the CI script that downloads the pinned Hugging Face model snapshots (`bin/ci/prime_hf_models.py`). `bin/ci/ingest/snapshots.py` validates those snapshots in other CI jobs. It calls the function `cache_context` of that script.
cells.What Tron does with it: The function `cache_context` prints the value in the `ci` field of the `cache_context` log line. Nothing else changes.

evidence: bin/ci/prime_hf_models.py:966 - cache_context builds a dict from os.environ.get for a fixed list of names; RUNNER_NAME is the last name (line 979); unset gives None
bin/ci/prime_hf_models.py:1015 - the dict goes into the ci field of the cache_event call with event name cache_context; cache_event only prints (lines 861-867)
bin/ci/prime_hf_models.py:1397 - main() of the download script calls cache_context(args.root, "prime")

rows.name: RUNNER_TEMP

problems.statement: CI scripts and CI (`bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh`, `bin/ci/background-check.sh`, `bin/ci/resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh` and 7 more files)
problems.code_says: The Tron cell says Reads and sets, but the Where cell does not say which files set the name. Only tests set it: bin/ci/test-background-check.sh, bin/ci/nix-cache/test_cache.py and bin/slice-tests/test_bench_refresh_workflow.py. No workflow and no CI script sets it. The cell also holds a count of files.

cells.Where: CI scripts and CI workflows (`bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh`, `bin/ci/background-check.sh`, `bin/ci/resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh` and other files). Tests of the CI scripts and of workflow steps set it, for example `bin/ci/test-background-check.sh`.
cells.What Tron does with it: `bench-refresh-ci.sh` writes its work files there. `background-check.sh` keeps its state there when `BACKGROUND_CHECK_DIR` is not set. `resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh` puts the link to its Nix build result there. The CI workflows keep job files there.

evidence: bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh:441 - derive_publication writes publication-base.json and publication-apply-state.txt under ${RUNNER_TEMP:?RUNNER_TEMP is required}; lines 491 and 694 do the same for the PR body and the health alert body, so these commands stop when the name is unset or empty

rows.name: ARCHFLAGS

cells.What Tron does with it: The makefile of iotools (a third-party hardware register tool kept in `bin/iotools-1.5`) adds the text to `CFLAGS`. The compile and link commands of the `iotools` program use `CFLAGS`.

evidence: bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile:36 - CFLAGS = -Wall -Werror $(DEFS) $(ARCHFLAGS) $(EXTRA_CFLAGS) ...; the makefile never assigns ARCHFLAGS, so make takes it from the environment or the command line
bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile:48 - the link command is $(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ iotools.o $(OBJS); the objects come from the built-in %.o rule of make, which also uses CFLAGS
git grep ARCHFLAGS - bin/iotools-1.5/Makefile is the only file with the name

rows.name: CABAL_DIR

cells.Where: No reader in Tron. CI workflows set it for cabal (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`, `.github/workflows/cpp-coverage.yml`, `.github/workflows/ingest-coverage.yml`).
cells.What Tron does with it: The workflows write it to the `GITHUB_ENV` file for the later steps of the job. cabal (the Haskell build tool) then keeps its files under the job workspace.

evidence: .github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml:211 - echo "CABAL_DIR=${{ github.workspace }}/.cabal" >> $GITHUB_ENV in the step that sets up the build environment

rows.name: CARGO_BUILD_JOBS

problems.statement: `bin/bsub-build` exports it in the remote build job. cargo (the Rust build tool) then runs at most that number of parallel jobs.
problems.code_says: The cell says "that number" but names no number. The script exports CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=$cores, where cores is REMOTE_BUILD_CORES or 16 when that is unset, the same number that the job reserves with rusage[cores=...]. env -i drops a value of the submitting shell.

cells.Where: No reader in Tron. `bin/bsub-build` exports it for cargo inside the LSF build job.
cells.What Tron does with it: `bin/bsub-build` sets it in the remote build job to the number of reserved cores (`REMOTE_BUILD_CORES`). A value from the submitting shell is replaced. cargo (the Rust build tool) then runs at most that number of parallel jobs.

evidence: bin/bsub-build:15 - cores=${REMOTE_BUILD_CORES:-16}
bin/bsub-build:53 - payload="export REMOTE=0 NPROC_BUILD=$cores CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=$cores;"
bin/bsub-build:65 - the remote command starts with env -i and passes only HOME, USER, TERM and LANG, so a CARGO_BUILD_JOBS of the submitting shell does not reach the job
bin/bsub-build:75 - bsub reserves the same number with -R rusage[mem=$mem,cores=$cores]
git grep CARGO_BUILD_JOBS - bin/bsub-build is the only file that names it outside this document

rows.name: CARGO_HOME

cells.Where: No reader in Tron. `rust/rust-toolchain.sh`, `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` and `bin/ci/test_run_cargo_test_binary.py` set it for cargo (the Rust build tool) and rustup (the Rust installer).
cells.What Tron does with it: `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` exports it before it installs or upgrades Rust with rustup. It writes an `export CARGO_HOME` line into `rust/rustenv` when it selects Rust in the checkout or in `$HOME`. The cargo wrapper `rust/run-cargo` sources that file when `IN_NIX_SHELL` is empty.

evidence: rust/rust-toolchain.sh:216 - install_rust exports CARGO_HOME=<root>/.cargo before it runs rustup-init and rustup; line 251 does the same in upgrade_rust
rust/rust-toolchain.sh:136 - create_rustenv_file writes export CARGO_HOME="<root>/.cargo" into rust/rustenv (line 140)

rust/rust-toolchain.sh:421 - create_rustenv_file runs for the checkout installation (also line 450 after a fresh install) and at line 432 for the $HOME installation; lines 396 and 441 write an empty rustenv for Nix Rust and for Rust on PATH
rust/run-cargo:37 - with IN_NIX_SHELL empty and rust/rustenv present, the script sources rust/rustenv before exec cargo

unresolved: ImageOS - why the workflow still sets it. No Tron file and no step script reads the name. The line was added in commit be14ba38b1 when the workflow used the action erlef/setup-beam, which is gone now. The source of the four actions that the workflow uses today (checkout, upload-artifact, find-comment, create-or-update-comment) at their pinned commits would show whether one of them reads ImageOS.
notes: All 12 rows are in section 7, so no row has a For cell and label_doubts is empty. Nine rows are graded correct: their statements hold at 7eddde7895, and the changes only apply house rules. Rule 11: every Where cell that began with 'Nothing in Tron.' now begins with 'No reader in Tron.' (ImageOS, CABAL_DIR, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS, the four CARGO_BUILD_RUST* rows, CARGO_HOME, CARGO_NET_OFFLINE). Rule 5: removed the counts '3 CI workflows' (CABAL_DIR), '3 files' (CARGO_HOME) and 'and 7 more files' (RUNNER_TEMP). Rule 9: ARCHFLAGS said 'adds the flags'; it now says 'adds the text', and it defines iotools the way the EXTRA_CFLAGS row does. Rule 10: CARGO_HOME used `rust/rustenv` without a definition; the cell now says that `rust/run-cargo` sources the file when IN_NIX_SHELL is empty. That cell has exactly 40 words when words are split at spaces. Three rows are graded imprecise. RUNNER_NAME: bin/ci/ingest/snapshots.py also calls cache_context, so the log line also appears in gcp-nix.yml jobs. RUNNER_TEMP: the row said 'Reads and sets' but did not say that only tests set it. CARGO_BUILD_JOBS: 'that number' named no number; it is the reserved core count, REMOTE_BUILD_CORES or 16. Facts left out on purpose. RUNNER_TEMP: three commands of bench-refresh-ci.sh (derive-publication, upsert-pr, reconcile-health) stop with the shell error 'RUNNER_TEMP is required' when the name is unset or empty, and the other two scripts fall back to TMPDIR and then /tmp; the cell is correct without this and adding it would bring it to the 40-word limit. CABAL_DIR: the setup step of ingest-coverage.yml also expands its own $CABAL_DIR to put <value>/bin on PATH and in GITHUB_PATH (lines 59 and 64). The step reads only the value that it has just exported, so the label stays 'Sets'. CARGO_HOME is the same case in rust/rust-toolchain.sh and nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix. Other rows of the same tables still begin with 'Nothing in Tron.' and still hold counts (for example CDPATH, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, GITHUB_ENV); they are outside this chunk. The GITHUB_WORKFLOW row, which reads through the same function as RUNNER_NAME, words its Where cell differently; the two rows could share one wording.
